mainEntity.name: What Should I Budget For a Home Addition?
mainEntity.text: What Should I Budget For a Home Addition?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Planning an addition is exciting, but figuring out the budget can be a huge source of stress. It’s about more than just a cost-per-square-foot estimate; you need to look at the total picture to avoid surprises.

First, understand that the final cost depends on the complexity. Are you adding a simple room or a two-story addition with a kitchen or bath? The latter involves more plumbing, electrical, and high-end finishes, which increases the price. Second, always—always—set aside a contingency fund. We recommend 10-20% of your total budget. In construction, especially with older homes, you never know what you'll find when you open up a wall. This fund covers those unforeseen issues without derailing your project. Finally, remember that costs like architectural design, engineering, and permits are part of the budget, too.

A professional can help you get a clear, realistic cost breakdown from the start. If you’re ready to take the next step, contact YOR Construction & Investments for a free consultation and estimate to get your project on solid financial ground.
